newsitem.title: USA: IRS removes U.S. farm-tax threat on contract sales.
newsitem.headline: IRS removes U.S. farm-tax threat on contract sales.

text.p: The Internal Revenue Service, responding to an uproar in farm country, said Tuesday farmers could file U.S. income taxes as usual and without the threat of huge tax bills from use of so-called forward contracts to sell grain.

"This is good news for farmers who want to comply with the tax law and properly report this income on their returns," said IRS Commissioner Margaret Richardson. "They should complete their 1996 returns as they have been doing in the past or as they have been directed to after an IRS audit."

Bills were pending in the House and Senate to defuse the controversey by making it clear that forward contracts, a popular merchandising tool for farmers, were excluded when the alternative minimum tax is calculated.

They were excluded in the past but Congress dropped the wording in the 1986 tax reform law -- an oversight, according to farm-state lawmakers who accused the IRS of over-reaching. The Clinton administration supports the legislative fix.
"Farmers should not be taxed on income they have not received. That defies all common sense," said Senator Byron Dorgan, D.-N.D., sponsor of one of the bills.
